MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  March 9, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:19 p.m., on Monday, March 9, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Battalion Chief Lawrence, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIAL

1.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: ROBERT MARQUEZ – F2M26-3
  Mayor Maloney and the City Council wished to commend and thank Water Utility
  Supervisor Robert Marquez who recently retired after 24 years of faithful and loyal service
  to the Utilities Department and the City of Alhambra. Mayor Maloney presented a
  Certificate of Service plaque to Mr. Marquez for his outstanding work for the City.

  Mr. MARQUEZ spoke regarding his time in the Utilities Department and thanked Council
  and Staff for his time with the City.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATIONS: 3 MINUTES PER
SPEAKER, 30 MINUTES TOTAL) – F2M26-4

1) Daniel CHAN, 428 W. Main St, spoke against noise disturbances to residents from the F45
  Gym.

2) Jennifer KING, 428 W. Main St., spoke against noise disturbances to residents from the F45
  Gym.

3-9-26
 3) Adrian PRECIADO spoke against federal immigration enforcement tactics by United States
  Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents and the negative impact on the
  Latino/Hispanic community.

4) Nathan CHAN, 110 W. Las Tunas Dr., San Gabriel, representing the Alhambra Main Street
  Collection Community, spoke against noise disturbances to residents from the F45 Gym.

PRESENTATIONS

2.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John Bwarie, presented an update on
  recent Chamber of Commerce activities. Mr. BWARIE reported on businesses returning
  and reopening in the City and reported on community events organized by the Chamber
  of Commerce such as the Lunar New Year event. He also spoke to the changing role of
  the Chamber and the various methods of outreach to local businesses and the City. He
  also reported on the Chamber’s changes to the Around Alhambra local newspaper. He
  spoke regarding the services provided by the Chamber and upcoming events to attract
  new businesses to Alhambra and to fill vacant properties.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE and Mr. BWARIE discussed vacant
  commercial storefronts in Alhambra and the Chamber’s efforts to attract new businesses
  such as bookstores. Councilmember MAZA thanked Mr. Bwarie and the Chamber for their
  continued efforts. Councilmember WANG and Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER
  discussed the Around Alhambra newspaper. Mayor MALONEY, Mr. BWARIE, and Ms.
  LEE discussed the variety of restaurants in Alhambra and ways the Chamber could
  partner with the City to attract visitors during the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

3.  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. R2M26-5 ACCEPTING THE 2026 CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN – F2M23-70, R2M26-5, M2M26-41

  Battalion Chief LAWRENCE delivered a staff report. Rob FLANER, with Black and Veatch,
  provided a presentation which is available in the City Clerk’s Office. In July 2024, the City
  of Alhambra initiated a planning process to prepare for and reduce the impacts of identified
  natural hazards, in accordance with federal requirements set forth in the Disaster
  Mitigation Act of 2000 (Public Law 106-390). The planning area for the Hazard Mitigation
  Plan encompasses the entire City of Alhambra. The result of the organizational efforts
  has been to produce a Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and the
  California Governor’s Office of Emergency Services (Cal OES) approved multi-hazard
  mitigation plan. Hazard mitigation is defined as any sustained action taken to reduce or
  eliminate long-term risk to life and property from a hazard event. Mitigation planning is the
  systematic process of learning about the hazards that can affect the community, setting
  clear goals, identifying appropriate actions, and following through with an effective
  mitigation strategy. The City of Alhambra Fire Department secured funding for developing
  the Hazard Mitigation Plan with a FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grant. The Plan
  presents the accumulated information in a unified framework to ensure a comprehensive
  and coordinated plan covering all departments within the City of Alhambra. The Plan
  was prepared in accordance with the Cal OES Local Hazard Mitigation Plan and FEMA

  2
3-9-26
   Region 9 preparation guidelines. The complete draft 2026 Alhambra Local Hazard
  Mitigation Plan can be found here:
  https://www.alhambraca.gov/DocumentCenter/View/7548/City-of-Alhambra-LHMP_Adoption-Draft_03092026

  Public Comment:  George Lance, via Zoom, asked on the involvement of Jewish
  people funding the plan.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE and Mr. FLANER discussed examples of
  structure and infrastructure actions in the Plan and mitigation methods addressing wildfire
  risks. Fire Chief RAGUSA also provided clarification regarding wildfire risk mitigation
  methods and ways to provide educational resources to the community. Councilmember
  MAZA and Mr. FLANER discussed wildfire risk mitigation and extreme heat risks to the
  population. Battalion Chief LAWRENCE also discussed methods to reduce extreme heat
  risks with Mr. MAZA. They went on to discuss flood risks in Alhambra and mitigation
  methods. Councilmember WANG and Mr. FLANER discussed the prioritization of actions
  in the Plan as well as which actions were already funded. Ms. WANG requested a list of
  priorities focusing on the impact on the community and Mr. LAWRENCE provided
  clarification. Ms. WANG went on to discuss seismic risks to critical city facilities with Mr.
  FLANER. Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. LAWRENCE discussed community
  cooling centers and wildfire risks from palm trees. Ms. LEE and Mr. LAWRENCE
  continued to discuss extreme heat risks and resources at cooling centers. Director of
  Parks and Recreation MACIAS provided clarification regarding the cooling center at the
  Joslyn Senior Center. Mayor MALONEY continued to discuss extreme heat risks,
  mitigation methods, and lower electricity blackout risks during heatwaves.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-5 entitled: A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Alhambra authorizing the adoption of the 2026
  Alhambra Local Hazard Mitigation Plan adopting the 2026 City of Alhambra Local Hazard
  Mitigation Plan; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the
  Council’s action. (M2M26-41)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 13): (TIME LIMITATIONS: 5 MINUTES PER SPEAKER
FOR ONE ITEM, 10 MINUTES PER SPEAKER FOR 2+ ITEMS)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 4, were considered by the
City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

4.  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT WITH
  CALTRANS FOR THE PA&ED, PS&E, AND R/W PHASES FOR THE FREMONT
  AVENUE INTERCHANGE PROJECT – F2M19-32, C2M26-17, M2M26-46

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. Staff requested the City Council
  authorize entering into a Cooperative Agreement, subject to review and approval by the
  City Manager and the City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and the
  California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) to complete the Project Approval and
  Environmental Document (PA&ED), PS&E (Plans, Specifications, and Estimate), and
  3
3-9-26
   Right-Of-Way (R/W) phases for the Fremont Avenue Interchange Project (Project). On
  March 2, 2026, the City of Alhambra received the Caltrans-approved PSR-PDS document
  for the Project. Approval of the PSR-PDS completes the project initiation phase and allows
  the Project to advance into the next stages of the Caltrans project development process,
  subject to execution of the proposed Cooperative Agreement with Caltrans for the PA&ED,
  PS&E, and R/W phases. During the PA&ED phase, the City, in coordination with Caltrans,
  would continue refining the Project’s purpose and need, evaluating and developing
  alternatives, conducting technical studies, and coordinating with partner agencies and the
  community. The PA&ED phase was a critical step in evaluating and refining alternatives
  that meet the Project’s purpose and need, including analysis of operational performance,
  safety considerations, environmental impacts, and cost. The key activities associated with
  the PA&ED and PS&E phases were summarized in the March 9, 2026 staff report by the
  Assistant City Manager and Director of Public Works & Utilities. As the Project advances
  into the PA&ED phase, project costs, public and stakeholders input, environmental
  impacts, and technical data will be further evaluated. The phase typically begins with a
  kickoff meeting with the Project Development Team (PDT). The kickoff meeting would
  outline roles and responsibilities and establishes coordination procedures for the PA&ED
  phase. It would also provide an opportunity to review the project schedule, confirm
  technical study requirements, and discuss the anticipated approach for public outreach
  and stakeholder engagement.

  Public Comment:
  The following people spoke against the Cooperative Agreement:
  1) Antonio Gardea, 2905 W. Norwood Pl.
  2) Gerry Fagoaga, 2020 S. Stoneman Ave.
  3) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St.
  4) Chris Olson, 915 N. Curtis Ave.
  5) David Bond
  6) Shirley Tatsuno, 1408 S. Fifth St.
  7) Ron Sahu, 311 N. Story Pl.
  8) Thomas Ferguson, 106 S. Chapel Ave.
  9) Meehar Tom, 1517 Commonwealth Ave.
  10) Sawyer Brooks, 118 E. McLean
  11) Marisol Grier, 815 Lindaraxa Park
  12) Dan Bednarski, via Zoom
  13) Melissa Michelson, via Zoom
  14) Michael Lawrence, via Zoom

  Discussion: Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST
  discussed the purpose of the cooperative agreement, the PSR/PDF process with
  CalTrans, and the objectives under the project. Eugene HUANG from Kimley-Horn
  provided further clarification regarding the PSR/PDF phase and the PAD/PSNE Right-of-
  Way Phases. They also discussed public comment regarding an Environmental Impact
  Report. Mr. HUANG provided clarification regarding the CalTrans project process and
  continued discussing the scoping process with Mayor MALONEY. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER further discussed the concerns of the public with Mr. HUANG.

  Councilmember WANG discussed the concerns of the public and supported their
  suggestion for a Town Hall meeting not tied to the CalTrans process. She continued to
  discuss concerns with funding allocation for the four major components of the project. Ms.
  WANG, Mr. HUANG, and Jason VALENCIA with KIMLEY-HORN discussed sequencing
  4
3-9-26
   of the project, CalTrans process, the funding allocation left for the freeway stub portion,
  and the proposed in depth traffic analysis study as each element relate to one another.
  Ms. WANG expressed concern with moving forward with the project without receiving
  clarification regarding how committing to the Fremont Interchange Project would impact
  the underfunded Stub Project. Mr. HUANG discussed project funding, funding comparison
  for different designs of the project, and potential funding partnerships. Ms. WANG and Mr.
  HUANG discussed the braided ramp design for the Fremont Ramp Project and traffic
  impact in the area.

  Councilmember MAZA supported the public suggestion for a Town Hall separate from a
  scoping meeting and addressed public concerns with transparency and funding. He also
  expressed concerns with the EIR process. Mr. MAZA and Mr. HUANG discussed project
  sequencing in prioritizing either the Fremont Ramp or the 710 Stub, the CalTrans project
  development process, funding assistance from CalTrans and potential funding
  partnerships, and the suggestion for a Town Hall meeting. Mr. MAZA and City Attorney
  MONTES discussed the process for a Town Hall meeting as a Council meeting or meeting
  without all members of Council present. Mr. HUANG clarified that the City was in a position
  to move forward with both the PSPDS for the 710 Stub and the PAD for the Fremont Ramp
  Project at the same time. Mr. MAZA and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the potential
  involvement with CalState Los Angeles with the 710 Stub. Mr. HUANG further discussed
  the potential Town Hall meeting without first conducting the next phase of studies and
  data collecting during the CalTrans scoping process.

  Councilmember LEE discussed the lack of support for the Fremont project, supported a
  Town Hall meeting in the form of a City Council meeting, and discussed the CalTrans
  process and authority over the City with Mr. HUANG. Council discussed traffic impacts
  and data with Mr. HUANG and Mr. VALENCIA. Ms. LEE suggested tabling the approval
  until after the Town Hall meeting in order to receive more public comment and due to
  concerns regarding CalTrans involvement.

  Mayor MALONEY discussed the background of the project including the braided Fremont
  Ramp and the 710 Stub, the unforeseen prolonged timeline, and questions regarding
  CalTrans involvement. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. HUANG discussed the scoping process,
  the EIR process, the cooperative agreement, the City’s design options for the Fremont
  Ramp and the 710 Stub, and the CalTrans project approval process. Mr. MALONEY
  further discussed his concerns with CalTrans approval process and the need for a
  preliminary informational meeting with CalTrans to address those concerns. He stated that
  he would prefer to have some answers before conducting a Town Hall meeting with the
  public.

  Ms. LEE motioned to table discussion. Mr. MALONEY supported the motion, and
  requested that the motion include a direction to staff to first meet with CalTrans to discuss
  concerns and then direct staff to return with a report for a Special City Council meeting.
  Mr. MONTES made suggestions for Ms. Lee to alter her motion and Ms. LEE agreed to
  the amendments to her motion. Council discussed scheduling and structure of the meeting
  to best receive public input. Mr. MAZA requested the motion specify that this would be an
  evening Special City Council meeting which would take place after discussion with
  CalTrans and CalState LA. Ms. LEE accepted the amendments.

  5
3-9-26
   Action Taken:  City Council tabled the Item, directed staff to set up a meeting with
  CalTrans to discuss concerns, and directed staff return with a report at a Special City
  Council meeting after.

  Vote:  Moved:  LEE  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  WANG, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON GLENAVEN
  AVENUE, ORANGE GROVE AVENUE, MIDWICK DRIVE, LA GOLONDRINA AVENUE,
  AND ROSS AVENUE – F2M24-64, N2M26-29

  The Sewer Master Plan identified the Sewer Replacement Project on Glenaven Avenue
  (from Glen View Dr. to Orange Grove Ave.), Orange Grove Avenue (from Glenaven Ave.
  to Midwick Dr.), Midwick Drive (from Orange Grove Ave. to West of Ramona Terrace),
  and at La Golondrina Avenue, and Ross Avenue as deficient in capacity. The existing
  12-inch pipe was expected to be surcharged during existing and ultimate peak wet
  weather conditions. A portion would be surcharged during existing and ultimate peak dry
  weather conditions. The Master Plan recommended replacement of the existing sewer
  main with a larger diameter sewer main. Plans and specifications were prepared. Staff
  reviewed the plans and found them to be consistent with the City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Sewer Replacement Project on Glenaven Avenue, Orange
  Grove Avenue, Midwick Drive, La Golondrina Avenue, and Ross Avenue, due no later
  than 10:30 a.m. on April 23, 2026 and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  AUTHORIZE RFP: CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT AND CONSTRUCTION
  INSPECTION SERVICES FOR POPLAR BOULEVARD REHABILITATION PROJECT
  (FEDERALLY FUNDED PROJECT STPL-5130(024)) – F2M25-55, RFP2M26-1

  On October 13, 2025, the City Council approved the circulation of the Notice of Inviting

  February 23, 2026, the City Council awarded the construction contract. The project
  consisted of cold milling and overlaying Poplar Blvd. from Main St. to the west City limit.
  Pursuant to the project, staff sought to distribute a Request for Proposals for Construction
  Management and Construction Inspection Services.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for Construction Management and Construction Inspection Services for the Poplar Blvd
  6
3-9-26
   Rehabilitation Project (Federally Funded Project STPL-5130(024)), with proposals due no
  later than 4:00 p.m. on April 9, 2026.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA

  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND SUPPORT
  SERVICES FOR THE POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M26-28, RFP2M26-2

  The Police Department has been using a contracted firm for Professional Information
  Technology and Support Services. The contract was due to expire on June 30, 2026. The
  Department sought a qualified firm with experience in the public safety field that would
  provide critical information technology and support services, with emphasis on mobile and
  wireless technology, networking infrastructure, service and application administration,
  programming, project management and backup and recovery solutions. The selected firm
  would also need to assist the Police Department with geographic information systems,
  computer aided dispatching, records management systems, body-worn camera and in-car
  camera systems, and various other public safety applications. The awarded contract
  would be for a five-year period from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for Professional Information Technology and Support Services for the Police Department;
  and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  APPROVAL OF A THIRD AMENDMENT TO THE CONTRACT WITH
  PERFORMANCE TRUCK REPAIR, INC. – F2M21-41, C2M21-35, M2M26-42

  On May 10, 2021, the City Council awarded a contract to Performance Truck Repair Inc.
  (PTR) for preventive maintenance and service repair for emergency fire apparatus in the
  Fire Department fleet in the amount of $265,000.00 annually. On June 27, 2022, the City
  Council approved an amendment to modify the amount to $365,000.00; and on April 14,
  2025, the City Council approved a second amendment to modify the amount to
  $465,000.00 annually. The contract was due to expire on June 30, 2026. Due to
  unforeseen major apparatus repairs and the age of the fleet, it was necessary to increase
  the contract by an additional $150,000.00 per year to continue the necessary maintenance
  and repairs for the remainder of the fiscal year, including a one-year extension. The Fire
  Department would like to continue to work with PTR. PTR has consistently been the lowest
  bidder in previous years, and they have agreed to continue their service at the same rate
  and terms set in 2021. Therefore, staff recommended the City Council award a one-year
  contract extension.

  Discussion:  None.

  7
3-9-26
   Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment to the contract between the
  City of Alhambra and Performance Truck Repair Inc. (Contract No. C2M21-35) for an
  additional amount of $150,000.00 to reflect a not to exceed amount of $615,000.00
  annually; extended the contract for one additional year, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-42)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  APPROVAL OF CONTRACT AMENDMENT WITH SHARP PERFORMANCE – F2M26-
  16, K2M25-314, M2M26-43

  On April 1, 2025, an agreement (K2M25-314) was established between City of Alhambra
  and Sharp Performance for the period of April 1, 2025, through March 31, 2026, which
  included the mobile app. Sharp Performance is a mental performance and coaching
  platform designed for professionals in high-risk occupations, such as law enforcement first
  responders. It was initially funded by the Officer Wellness grant in the amount of $34,800.
  The Department has continued to show steady increase in utilization of Sharp
  Performance with 64% of sworn staff onboarded. Sharp Performance remains reliable and
  consistent and has demonstrated an understanding of our goal: to continue providing
  ongoing support to our sworn personnel. Staff sought to extend the agreement for a two-
  year period from April 1, 2026, through March 31, 2028, for an additional $71,200 for a
  total contract price of $106,000. Sole source purchase is allowable per Municipal Code
  3.36.080 Section (B)(2). The JPIA would reimburse $15,000 per fiscal year for this
  extension.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an Amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Contract No. K2M25-314 between
  Sharp Performance and the City of Alhambra for its mobile application platform; extend
  the agreement through March 31, 2028; authorized the Chief of Police to execute said
  agreement; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s
  action. (M2M26-43)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  CONTRACT AUTHORIZATIONS FOR THE PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF THE
  JAIL AND STATION CONTROLLER SYSTEM – F2M26-6B, C2M26-15, C2M26-16,
  M2M26-44

  The Police Department Jail Controller System was upgraded in 2016. The system was
  out of warranty and was no longer supported by the vendor. In addition, there were some
  malfunctions that required manual workarounds. Staff contacted three vendors to assess
  repair or replacement options. One vendor submitted a proposal of $178,836.99; one
  vendor was unable to provide a quote due to component limitations; and Intelli-Tech and
  8
3-9-26
   Adrazen Networks submitted a combined proposal of $119,612.93. Due to the urgent need
  to secure jail and facility access operations, staff recommended proceeding with Intelli-
  Tech and Adrazen’s proposal in the amount of $119,612.93. The Department would
  purchase the equipment required directly from Intelli-Tech in the amount of $54,400.26
  and Adrazen would complete the installation in the amount of $65,212.67. Emergency
  procurement is allowable under Alhambra Municipal Code Section 3.36.070, which
  authorizes emergency purchases when a breakdown in machinery or an essential service
  requires immediate action to protect public health, welfare, or safety.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded two contracts, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney for the procurement and installation of the
  Jail Controller System to Intelli-Tech (procurement) in the amount of $54,400.26 and to
  Adrazen Networks (installation) in the amount of $65,212.67; authorized the Chief of
  Police to execute said agreements; directed the Finance Director to complete a budget
  transfer of $88,986.90 to the Capital Outlay Fund and to appropriate an additional
  $30,626.03 from the Capital Outlay Fund to complete the project, for a total project cost of
  $119,612.93; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M26-44)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT WITH MOTOROLA SOLUTIONS, INC. FOR COMPUTER
  AIDED DISPATCH AND RECORDS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM (RMS) FOR THE
  POLICE DEPARTMENT – F2M18-6B, C2M18-66, M2M26-45

  On December 13, 2018, the City entered into contract no. C2M18-66 for the purchase of
  the public safety Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System
  (RMS) for a total of $1,127,388.85 under a five-year lease. By 2020, the CAD/RMS was
  implemented, and it included a free year and one month of maintenance through June 30,
  2026. On June 27, 2022, the City Council approved a Contract Amendment to C2M18-66
  for various enhancements and based on the amendment, another $90,286.64 in contract
  costs were authorized, bringing the total contract amount to $1,217,675.49. Through June
  30, 2026, the expected expenditures for the CAD/RMS support services contract were
  identified as $1,201,611.49, which was under the authorized amount. Currently, the
  system has operated on the 2022 version but needed an upgrade (server migration). This
  upgrade would be included in the five-year support and maintenance costs, which when
  annualized are for an additional $540,860.93 for a contract total not to exceed
  $1,742,472.42 after adding the year-to-date actuals to the projected five-year costs. The
  contract would expire on June 30, 2026 and staff recommended dispensing with the
  competitive bid process under Municipal Code 3.38.050 to avoid operational disruptions.
  Due to the complexity of the current systems and the time required to transition to a new
  vendor, such change would likely cause delays and service interruptions, negatively
  impacting operations.

  Discussion:  None.

  9
3-9-26
   Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment with Motorola
  Solutions, Inc. (C2M18-66), subject to final language and approval by the City Attorney
  and the City Manager, for an additional five-years of service with Motorola Solutions, Inc.
  for Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) and Records Management System (RMS) (through
  June 30, 2031) at an additional cost of $540,860.93 (for a contract total not to exceed
  $1,742,472.42); authorized the Chief of Police to execute the said amendment; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-
  45)

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

13.  DEMANDS - F2M26-1

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved as submitted Final Check List (264844 thru
  264970 and 1048 thru 1048) in the amount of $744,082.08 and EFT’s in the amount of
  $179,983.09 for the period ending February 19, 2026 and Schedule of Wire Transfers in
  the amount of $557,769.69 for the week ending February 13, 2026; and, Final Check List
